subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Langston Hughes's 1926 poem "Mother to Son."

Well, son, I'll tell you:
Life for me ain't been no crystal stair.
It's had tacks in it,
And splinters,
And boards torn up,
And places with no carpet on the floor—
Bare.
But all the time
I'se been a-climbin' on,
And reachin' landin's,
And turnin' corners,
And sometimes goin' in the dark
Where there ain't been no light.
So boy, don't you turn back.
Don't you set down on the steps
'Cause you finds it's kinder hard.
Don't you fall now—
For I'se still goin', honey,
I'se still climbin',
And life for me ain't been no crystal stair.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To express hope that a child will follow the exact same path as his parent did
choices.B: To describe the physical deterioration of an old staircase in a building
choices.C: To warn a child that life will be filled with insurmountable obstacles
choices.D: To encourage a child to persevere despite the difficulties life will present

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it accurately states the text's main purpose. The poem begins with the speaker describing her own difficult journey through life, using the metaphor of a worn staircase with "tacks" and "splinters." The speaker then explains that despite these hardships, she has kept "climbin' on" and "reachin' landin's." Finally, she directly urges her son not to "turn back" or "set down" when he finds life difficult. Thus, the main purpose is to encourage a child to persevere despite the difficulties he will face in life.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the speaker encourages the child to keep climbing and not give up ("don't you turn back") without suggesting that he should follow her exact same path or experiences.
